style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: Not to us -- the psalm that gives glory back to God and mocks the idols that cannot take it. It opens with the line the Reformation distilled into its watchword, Soli Deo Gloria: not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to Your name give glory. The occasion is a taunt: the nations ask, 'Where is their God?' -- and the answer is that He is in the heavens doing exactly what He pleases, while their gods are on earth, silver and gold, handmade, with mouths that do not speak, eyes that do not see, ears, noses, hands, feet, throats, all inert. The devastating line is the eighth: those who make them become like them, and so does everyone who trusts them. Then a threefold call -- Israel, the house of Aaron, the God-fearers: trust in the LORD; He is their help and shield -- answered by a threefold blessing over the same three groups, small and great together. The heavens are the LORD's; the earth He has handed to the children of men. And the dead do not praise Him -- so we, the living, will bless Him from now on and forever. Hallelujah.

1.text: Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to Your name give the glory, for the sake of Your covenant love and Your faithfulness.
1.amp: Not unto us, O LORD [YHWH], not unto us, but unto Your name [shem] give [natan] glory [kabod], for Your mercy [chesed -- covenant love], and for Your truth's [emeth -- faithfulness] sake.
1.notes: lo lanu YHWH, lo lanu -- 'not to us, O LORD, not to us' -- the double refusal that medieval Christendom sang as Non nobis, Domine, and that the Reformation distilled into Soli Deo Gloria: glory redirected to the shem (H8034), the Name, on the ground of chesed and emeth (H2617, H571). kabod (H3519) is weight; the psalm declines to carry any of it.

2.text: Why should the nations be saying, 'Where is their God now?'
2.amp: Wherefore should the heathen [goy] say [amar], Where is now their God [Elohim]?
2.notes: The taunt of the goyim (H1471): ayyeh-na Elohehem (H430) -- 'so where is this God of theirs?' The question every visible defeat of God's people invites (cf. Psalm 42:3; Joel 2:17), and the psalm answers it with an address: in the heavens, invisible, and unbothered.

3.text: But our God is in the heavens; all that He pleases, He has done.
3.amp: But our God [Elohim] is in the heavens [shamayim]: He has done [asah] whatsoever He has pleased [chaphets -- delighted in, willed].
3.notes: The Bible's plainest statement of sovereignty: Elohenu ba-shamayim, kol asher-chaphets asah (H8064, H2654, H6213) -- our God is in the heavens; everything He delights in, He has done. Invisible is not absent; the God the nations cannot find is the only one actually acting (cf. Psalm 135:6; Daniel 4:35).

4.text: Their idols are silver and gold, things made by the hands of men.
4.amp: Their idols [atsab -- fashioned images, things toiled over] are silver [keseph] and gold [zahab], the work [maaseh] of men's [adam] hands [yad].
4.notes: atsabbehem (H6091): the noun for idol shares its letters with the verbs 'to fashion' and 'to grieve, toil' -- the lexicons differ on whether that is derivation or wordplay, but either way these are gods that had to be manufactured. keseph ve-zahab (H3701, H2091), precious material; maaseh yede adam (H4639, H3027, H120), the product of a workshop. Isaiah 44 is the long version of this verse.

5.text: A mouth they have, but they do not speak; eyes they have, but they do not see;
5.amp: They have mouths [peh], but they speak [dabar] not: eyes [ayin] have they, but they see [raah] not:
5.notes: The inventory of a corpse: peh (H6310) without dabar (H1696), ayin (H5869) without raah (H7200). The satire is anatomical -- every organ present, every function absent -- and the LORD of verse 3, who has no visible body, does all of it.

6.text: ears, but cannot hear; noses, but cannot smell;
6.amp: They have ears [ozen], but they hear [shama] not: noses [aph] have they, but they smell [ruach -- catch a scent] not:
6.notes: ozen (H241) without shama (H8085) -- the idol cannot receive prayer, which is the whole reason to have one. aph (H639) that cannot ruach (H7306): the same word that elsewhere names the heat of God's anger, here a nose that cannot even detect the incense burned under it.

7.text: hands, but cannot feel; feet, but cannot walk; they make no sound in their throats.
7.amp: They have hands [yad], but they handle [mush -- feel, touch] not: feet [regel] have they, but they walk [halak] not: neither speak [hagah -- murmur, mutter] they through their throat [garon].
7.notes: yad (H3027) without mush (H4184), regel (H7272) without halak (H1980) -- and the closing detail: lo-yehgu bi-geronam (H1897, H1627), not even a murmur in the throat. hagah is the sound of Psalm 1's meditation; the idol cannot manage a hum.

8.text: Those who make them will become like them -- and so will everyone who trusts in them.
8.amp: They that make [asah] them are like unto them; so is every one that trusts [batach] in them.
8.notes: The psalm's theology of worship in one sentence: kemohem yihyu osehem (H6213) -- the makers become what they make -- and kol asher-boteach bahem (H982), every truster too. We grow into the likeness of what we trust: dead gods make deaf, blind, mute people (cf. 2 Corinthians 3:18 for the same law running the other way).

9.text: Israel, put your trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield.
9.amp: O Israel [Yisrael], trust [batach] in the LORD [YHWH]: He is their help [ezer] and their shield [magen].
9.notes: The alternative to verse 8: Yisrael betach ba-YHWH (H3478, H982, H3068) -- the same trust-verb, aimed at a living object. ezram u-maginnam (H5828, H4043), help and shield -- the refrain of verses 9-11: what an idol with hands cannot do, He does.

10.text: House of Aaron, put your trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield.
10.amp: O house [bayith] of Aaron [Aharon], trust [batach] in the LORD [YHWH]: He is their help [ezer] and their shield [magen].
10.notes: The second ring: bet Aharon (H1004, H175), the priests -- the same three circles Psalm 118:2-4 summons. Even the men who handle the holy things are told where to lean; office is not trust.

11.text: You who fear the LORD, put your trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield.
11.amp: Ye that fear [yare] the LORD [YHWH], trust [batach] in the LORD: He is their help [ezer] and their shield [magen].
11.notes: The third ring, open to anyone: yire YHWH (H3373), the God-fearers, the category the Gentile converts of Acts walked into. Three calls, one refrain -- the congregation answering each summons with 'help and shield' (H5828, H4043).

12.text: The LORD has kept us in mind, and He will bless us: He will bless the house of Israel; He will bless the house of Aaron;
12.amp: The LORD [YHWH] has been mindful [zakar] of us: He will bless [barak] us; He will bless the house [bayith] of Israel [Yisrael]; He will bless the house of Aaron [Aharon].
12.notes: The trust of verses 9-11 answered in the same three circles: YHWH zekharanu (H2142), He has remembered us -- and yevarekh (H1288), 'He will bless', three times. The idol with ears could not hear; the LORD not only heard but remembered, and blessing is what His memory does.

13.text: Those who fear the LORD He will bless -- the small ones together with the great.
13.amp: He will bless [barak] them that fear [yare] the LORD [YHWH], both small [qatan] and ['with', the KJV margin] great [gadol].
13.notes: The third blessing, and its reach: ha-qetannim im-ha-gedolim (H6996, H1419) -- the small WITH the great, one blessing for the child and the elder, the beggar and the king. God's favor does not scale with the recipient's size.

14.text: May the LORD increase you more and more, you and your children.
14.amp: The LORD [YHWH] shall increase [yasaph -- add to] you more and more, you and your children [ben].
14.notes: yoseph YHWH alekhem (H3254): may the LORD ADD to you -- Joseph's name is this verb -- alekhem ve-al-benekhem (H1121), upon you and upon your children. Blessing in the Old Testament is generational by default.

15.text: Blessed are you by the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.
15.amp: Ye are blessed [barak] of the LORD [YHWH] which made [asah] heaven [shamayim] and earth [eretz].
15.notes: berukhim attem la-YHWH (H1288), 'blessed are you by the LORD' -- and the credential that separates Him from verse 4's gods: oseh shamayim va-aretz (H6213, H8064, H776), Maker of heaven and earth. The idols were made; He makes. A blessing from the Maker of the universe, not from a product of a workshop.

16.text: The heavens are the LORD's own heavens, but the earth He has given to the children of men.
16.amp: The heaven [shamayim], even the heavens, are the LORD'S [YHWH]: but the earth [eretz] has He given [natan] to the children [ben] of men [adam].
16.notes: ha-shamayim shamayim la-YHWH (H8064) -- the heavens are the LORD's heavens -- ve-ha-aretz natan li-bene adam (H776, H5414, H1121, H120): earth handed to humanity as a stewardship, Genesis 1:28 restated. The answer to verse 2's 'where is their God?' is also a job description for His people.

17.text: It is not the dead who praise the LORD, nor any of those going down into the silence;
17.amp: The dead [muth] praise [halal] not the LORD [Yah], neither any that go down [yarad] into silence [dumah].
17.notes: lo ha-metim yehalelu-Yah (H4191, H1984, H3050): the dead do not praise -- and yorde dumah (H3381, H1745), those going down into the silence: Sheol as the place where the choir stops. Not a denial of afterlife but a plea about THIS life: praise is a living activity, and the psalmist means to keep doing it (cf. Psalm 6:5; Isaiah 38:18-19).

18.text: But we -- we will bless the LORD from now on and for all time. Praise the LORD!
18.amp: But we will bless [barak] the LORD [Yah] from this time forth and for [ad] evermore [olam]. Praise [halal] the LORD [Yah].
18.notes: va-anachnu nevarekh Yah (H1288, H3050) -- but WE, the living, will bless -- me-attah ve-ad-olam (H5704, H5769), 'from now and on to forever', Psalm 113:2's formula closing the loop. The idol-makers became like their idols (v. 8); the God-trusters become like their God: alive, speaking, praising. halelu-Yah (H1984).
